# Jobs dashboard

Every scheduled job on xero (and later the wol Pi) as a `systemd --user`
timer, with each run's start, duration, result, CPU, RAM and peak temperatures
exported to Prometheus for a Grafana "Jobs" dashboard - plus 60-day p50/p95/max
per job, to tell CPU-heavy from RAM-heavy jobs and schedule them apart.
`PROJECTS.md` entry: **"Jobs dashboard in Grafana"** (plan, review, decisions).

**Dashboard:** Grafana -> Homelab -> **Jobs** (`https://xero.<tailnet>/grafana/`, uid `jobs`), generated by `services/grafana/build_dashboards.py`.

**Status:** every job in xero's crontab runs from a timer since 2026-11-19
(phase 1; `tinxy-watchdog` was the pilot on 2026-11-18). The crontab keeps only
the 25 Nov Diwali one-off. Still to come: scrub/TRIM, the Pi, container jobs
(`tracker/jobs-dashboard.md`).

## What runs it

| Piece | Host | Started by |
|---|---|---|
| `jobs.toml` | - | the list of jobs, the only file to edit |
| `install_jobs.py` | each host | you, after editing `jobs.toml` |
| `job-<name>.timer` / `.service` | each host | generated into `~/.config/systemd/user/`, enabled by `install_jobs.py` |
| `record_run.sh` | each host | every job unit's last `ExecStartPre` (`start`: a sampler in the job's cgroup reads `cpu.stat` and `memory.stat` each second) and its `ExecStopPost` (saves the run's peak memory, peak RAM and highest 1s CPU %) |
| `jobs_collector.py` | each host | the `job-jobs-collector` timer, every minute at :30 |
| `test_jobs_collector.py` | - | you, after changing the collector: `python3 -m unittest projects/jobs-dashboard/test_jobs_collector.py` |
| `noop` job | xero | its timer, every 5 min: runs `/bin/true`, so its row is the hooks' own cost (the floor under every job) |
| `crontab.xero.before` | - | xero's crontab before any job moved: the rollback copy |

State and output:
- **Metrics:** `services/node-exporter/textfile/jobs.prom` (`homelab_job_*`), read by node-exporter.
- **Run history:** `~/.local/state/jobs-dashboard/runs/<job>.jsonl`, the last 60 days, one line per run (`duration`, `cpu`, `ram`, `mem`, `cpu_max`, `temps`). Every p50/p95/max comes from here, per run, never from averaging.
- **Stats cache:** `~/.local/state/jobs-dashboard/stats.json`, each job's summary of its history. Counts, maxima and failures update with every run; p50/p95 and the per-day CPU totals are recomputed from the file hourly, one job per collector run. Deleting it is safe: it is rebuilt from the history files.

#### Per-job stats (60 days)
| Field | Metric stem | Counts runs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duration | `homelab_job_duration_{p95,max}_seconds` | all | |
| CPU seconds | `homelab_job_cpu_{p50,p95,max}_seconds` | all | whole process tree; sub-second jobs are mostly hook overhead (Traps) |
| CPU per day | `homelab_job_cpu_busiest_day_seconds`, `..._cpu_last_24h_seconds` | all | sums, by IST day; hourly |
| Busiest second | `homelab_job_cpu_busiest_second_{p50,p95,max}_percent` | 1 s or more | % of one core |
| RAM | `homelab_job_ram_{p50,p95,max}_bytes` | all (since 2026-11-26) | anon, no page cache |
| Memory incl. cache | `homelab_job_memory_{p50,p95,max}_bytes` | all | `memory.peak` |
| Temperature | `homelab_job_temp_{p50,p95,max}_celsius{sensor}` | 60 s or more | `cpu`, `ssd_data` (Kingston), `ssd_boot` |

p50/p95 appear once a field has 20 runs; max from the first.
- **Job output:** appended to the same log file as under cron (`log` in `jobs.toml`), plus `journalctl --user -u job-<name>`.

## Add or move a job

1. Add a `[[job]]` to `jobs.toml` (field list at the top of the file). `systemd-analyze calendar '<on_calendar>'` shows when it will run; cron's `*/5` is `*:0/5`.
2. `projects/jobs-dashboard/install_jobs.py --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`.
3. **Moving from cron:** delete the crontab line in the same step, or the job runs twice:
   `crontab -l | grep -v '<script path>' | crontab -`
4. Check: `systemctl --user list-timers 'job-*'`; after the first run, `projects/jobs-dashboard/jobs_collector.py --print | grep <name>`.

Removing a job from `jobs.toml` and re-running `install_jobs.py` stops and deletes its units. Units without the `GENERATED` header are never touched.

## Roll back

```
crontab projects/jobs-dashboard/crontab.xero.before   # cron as it was
# then remove the moved jobs from jobs.toml (keep jobs-collector) and:
projects/jobs-dashboard/install_jobs.py
```

## Traps

- **No network ordering in user units.** `After=network-online.target` does nothing there; set `network = true` and the unit waits for a default route in `ExecStartPre`.
- **systemd 255 forgets `MemoryPeak` when a oneshot unit stops** (kept from 256). That is why `record_run.sh` reads `memory.peak` in `ExecStopPost`.
- **Max CPU / 1s CPU % is % of one core** (100 = one full core; xero has 4, so up to 400), the highest 1s sample of the run (since 2026-11-24; before that the column was total CPU seconds). The sampler costs ~1% of a core. **A run under a second** gets its whole-run rate, which includes the hooks' own few ms, so tiny jobs read 50-100% (`/bin/true` reads ~60-90%) - that is short, not heavy. The 60-day 1s CPU % stats skip runs under a second.
- **CPU seconds of sub-second jobs are mostly our own hooks** (`record_run.sh` and the sampler run inside the job's cgroup; ~0.03 s a run). Compare a job with the `noop` row before calling it heavy.
- **`memory.peak` counts page cache:** a job that reads big files (backup-documents: 328 MB) looks big without needing the RAM. Scheduling decisions use **RAM** (`anon` of `memory.stat`, sampled each second). A run under a second is never sampled and records `memory.peak` as its RAM, an upper bound (such runs are a few MB).
- **No disk I/O numbers:** the `io` cgroup controller is not delegated to user units (`cpu memory pids` only).
- **Whole-second timestamps:** `ExecMainStartTimestamp` is rounded to the second, so durations use the `...Monotonic` (microsecond) properties.
- **Work done via `docker exec` is charged to the container**, not the job, so CPU and memory undercount jobs that mostly drive containers.
- **Temperatures** are looked up in Prometheus over the run window (at least 10s, since the scrape is every 5s). drivetemp's `target0` is the Kingston (`datapool`), `target1` the BIWIN boot SSD (checked 2026-11-18); a disk swap can change that.
- **The collector records its own runs itself** (`record_self`, from `getrusage`): systemd always shows it mid-run, never finished. It also reports itself as not running (or every minute would be shaded on the graphs).
- **The collector runs at :30, not :00.** It sees only each unit's latest run; an every-minute job still running when it looks would be skipped if the next run had started by the next look.
- **History files only grow by appending, and are not re-read every minute.** Every-minute jobs reach ~86k runs in 60 days (~0.6s to read). The collector reads a file only for its hourly recompute (one job per run, the stalest), dropping runs past 60 days once a day; the run's temperatures are looked up before it is appended. One `systemctl show` covers every unit. Together: ~0.2 CPU-s a run, down from 0.6 (2026-11-26).
- **healthcheck ignores failed `job-*` units.** A failed run leaves its unit failed until the next run; alerting on that is a separate decision (alerting stayed unchanged, 2026-11-18). Failures show on the dashboard.
- **`glacier-archive` keeps `flock -n`** so a manual run (`projects/immich-backup/README.md`) cannot overlap the timer's; relative paths in `command` resolve from the repo root (`WorkingDirectory`).
- **The label is `name`, not `job`:** Prometheus sets `job` to the scrape job (`node`) and renames a clashing label to `exported_job`.
